summary.title: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education
summary.one_liner: You learn practical tool proficiency for computer science work: the command line, text editors, version control with Git, debugging and profiling, and packaging code.
keywords: how to learn command line tools
takeaways: Covers shell and command-line environment skills that classes usually skip
Includes lectures on development environments, debugging and profiling, and Git version control
Covers packaging and shipping code, agentic coding with AI tools, and code quality in the 2026 syllabus
Older special topics include data wrangling, security and cryptography, backups, automation, and web and browsers
Course materials and lecture notes are freely available, with community translations listed
summary.summary: This MIT course site presents a set of lectures on developer tooling that are usually left for students to learn on their own. The 2026 syllabus runs from January 12 to 23 and covers the shell, command-line environment, development environment and tools, debugging and profiling, version control with Git, packaging and shipping code, agentic coding, beyond the code, and code quality. The page says AI tools are folded into each lecture rather than taught in a standalone lecture. It also lists special topics from earlier years (such as data wrangling and security and cryptography) and links to community translations and discussion channels.
